traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Crassulaceae (read 2026-10-17): blade usually undivided, cut (pinnatifid) in some Bryophyllum and Kalanchoe. Wikipedia: margins sometimes broadly lobed or more deeply incised. Sedum, Crassula, Echeveria leaves undivided (genus weighting).

traits.leaf_margin.note: Wikipedia, Crassulaceae (read 2026-10-17): margin mostly smooth, otherwise crenate to broadly lobed, at times dentate. DELTA, Crassulaceae (read 2026-10-17): margins entire, crenate or serrate.

traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 297, 299: stamens once or twice the petal number (5 or 5+5, rarely from 3 to more than 6 per whorl).

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 299: gynoecium of 5 free carpels, rarely 3 to 6 or more.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 297, 505: flowers hypogynous or slightly perigynous, so a small floral cup in some. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 298 Crassulaceae: herbs or undershrubs, usually succulent; leaves opposite or alternate, without stipules; flowers regular, bisexual, usually in cymes; sepals often 4 or 5, petals as many, free or joined; stamens as many or twice as many as the petals; carpels superior, as many as the petals, free or joined at the base; fruit of follicles opening on the inner side. Library 1.0 draws 86% of the family as succulents; their habit is the growth form's, not stated here.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Crassulaceae: how long the leaves last (character 37), coded evergreen. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Crassulaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded often a basal rosette, often no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Crassulaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 299, 300, family Crassulaceae: leaf division simple; read as "simple".

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 299, 300, family Crassulaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite, usually; read as {"hermaphrodite": "usually"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add solitary (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 299, 300: branched cyme, or flowers solitary.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Wikipedia Crassulaceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves opposite-decussate or alternate-spiral; Sedum (largest genus, c. 300-500 spp.) alternate, Echeveria (c. 150) in the alternate Sempervivoideae; Crassula (c. 200) and the Kalanchoe clade (c. 130-240) opposite. DELTA (read 2026-10-17): alternate, opposite or whorled. Alternate genera (Sedum, Echeveria, Telephiinae c. 150, Aeonium, Sempervivum) outnumber the opposite ones. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.
